result.title: Rethinking Fixed-Horizon Latent Reasoning
result.summary: Existing latent reasoners typically run for a preset latent horizon during inference. Intuitively, a longer horizon should provide more opportunity for reasoning. However, in this work, we find that extending latent Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to the full preset horizon may in fact degrade reasoning performance. We observe that latent CoT evolves through distinct functional stages, with earlier computation forming frontier reasoning states, while later computation mainly reorganizes existing candidates and can weaken gold candidate support. These findings motivate a rethink of fixed-horizon latent inference. To address this, we characterize the reasoning benefits of latent CoT by realized and remaining constructive progress. Empirically, we find that higher realized constructive progress corresponds to higher current reasoning accuracy, while more remaining progress corresponds to larger future gains from continued latent CoT. To this end, we introduce a lightweight method that estimates the remaining reasoning progress and adaptively adjusts the latent horizon during inference. Across representative latent CoT reasoners and multiple arithmetic benchmarks, our method improves reasoning accuracy by up to 7.2 percentage points while reducing latent computation by up to 29.0%, without retraining the LLM.

AI.brief_summary: 论文发现固定长度 latent CoT 并非越长越好：早期计算形成前沿推理状态，后期主要在重组已有候选甚至削弱正确候选支持；据此提出以「已实现/剩余构造性进展」刻画收益，并用轻量估计器在推理时自适应调整 latent 步数，无需重训即可提分并减少计算。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 THINK/STOP 的收益—成本权衡与 latent 状态演化假设，其对后期计算是否有效、如何判定停止的结论可供核查是否与「预测工作区」类解释一致。
